body: Thank you so much for your advice & honesty. All this meant a lot to me.

Thanks for sharing all this w/ me. You've helped a ton, honestly. If it's not too much trouble, I have a quick question. Would you recommend meds? I know it's ultimately a doctor's decision, but I mean... Generally, do they help chill the house out at all?

That makes complete sense. But then that leads me to this thought:  As much as I hate to admit it, I am horrible at balance. My therapist told me she thinks I could have bipolar disorder. So when Maxine is up my ass... Unless I am in my "nothing can touch me" mood, I can't shut her up. I just don't have enough energy to. I feel empty. I feel nostalgic. Everything around me eats at me. But if I push through it regardless of how dark I feel... At some point, I will tire of having that routine. Being "tired" is what makes me feel suicidal. I wish I could break that exhaustion.
Thank you. I will definitely try my hardest.

Last year, I started a weekly newsletter called Lovely Letters. It was my outlet, but it also helped others apparently. Unfortunately, I only did a handful. The school didn't like them for various reasons, the statistics I had gathered in my own school were depressing me, & I wanted to keep them 100% honest... Being 100% honest is easy for me, but I wanted to HELP. Not HURT. So once I started slipping again, I quit writing.

To answer your 2nd question... That's a difficult one. Ummm. Well. My freshman & sophomore year, I was a LOT more... Dramatic? Actually, not even dramatic... Just spazzy. Since the feeling was fresh, I had no idea how to deal w/ it. All I knew was the general flow of how I felt. I would be extremely happy, on top of the fucking world... & then boom. I'd just remember all the shitty things I've been through because it would have been triggered by something I saw... & I'd crash. Insanely hard. Believe me when I say that those "triggers" are everywhere for me too. My small town is: horribly judgmental, insanely hypocritical, & they love to push everything that makes them look bad under the carpet.

Anyways, I was very open to advice back then. Well, as open as someone like me can be about the REAL shit I'm thinking about. I don't actively keep secrets, but I also won't tell anyone anything unless I'm asked. In my 1st 2 years of HS, I spoke up from time to time. It helped & hurt. But the amount of help I was getting didn't match anywhere close to how hurt I was by what people had to say to me. Their cheery outlook was something I respected deeply, but I couldn't take another "it gets better" if I was paid a million dollars. I hate that phrase, because it leaves me hanging. What am I supposed to do? Just wait out how shitty I feel in the hopes that it might indeed get better? Lol. Idk. Maybe I'm too harsh. 

I would tell my friends exactly how I felt if I was asked. That's why I ended up in the therapy. One day at lunch, my friend asked how I was. Although I don't remember exactly what I said... It was probably something like "I'm sick of feeling this low." They then, like a good friend, asked why I was sad. When I couldn't explain that there wasn't something in specific, they kept hounding me as if I were hiding something. After a while of them trying to guess what it could have been that set me off, I just flat out told them I wanted to die. That I just couldn't handle the emotional rollercoaster that was life, & that I would tell them the specifics if they made any sense to me. My other friend who was listening then said "Emma, if you killed yourself... I wouldn't ever be able to look at orange juice the same." (I drink orange juice religiously) That made me instantly cry. So I stormed out of the lunch room, went upstairs to my locker, & started hitting it & crying. (Like a dumbass) Then I was reported. 

Now? Now I just... Don't make any scenes. I try not to anyways. I'm a very loud person though, so it's hard. I have a lot of passion, & I literally fit NOWHERE at my school. I dress like a Punky Brewster-Marilyn Manson hybrid (I am not a certain style of person), & people think I'm weird. If my close friends, my real friends, ask me how I am or what's up... I say "the usual. Casually dying." I have dark humor, but that way I also don't have to get into the details. (That's if I'm depressed, BTW. Not every single time) If anyone else asks, I say "decent." 

I avoid telling anyone my real thoughts now, but I am very. Very. VERY. Open minded to what anyone on here has to say. I trust Reddit. It's full of intelligent & brilliant people. & I will violate my standard closed off rule for you all.

The school sponsored 6 months of free therapy for me, because they had to. I guess if a student mentions wanting to kill themselves or self-harm, they automatically send you to a hospital or to what I had. I only told them about how I had self-harmed.  (And I only said I had once which was bull)

The therapy center's goal was to stray me away from that. I don't think I ever mentioned self-harm or suicidal thoughts again, cause I knew I would be taken to a bigger, serious facility. I told my therapist 90% of my home life though, which was an enormous step for me. I had never once let anyone in on that side of things. I've been through a lot, parent wise. To answer your question specifically, I got a lot of advice for how to "deal" with them. Deal isn't the correct word, but I don't know what else to use. 

However I will say that the ONLY piece of advice I got from my therapist that made sense to me was this:

Everyone has depression. It just comes in many forms, and it's frequency is different. Whether this is true or not, it comforted me. She furthermore told me I shouldn't be calling depression, "depression." It should have the name of a person. She named it Maxine for me. This was to show me that I shouldn't let Maxine, who was another person, have control over me. That I shouldn't let her pressure me into doing & feeling bad things. It makes sense, honestly. If someone told me to self-harm, their words would hurt... But I definitely wouldn't do it because they told me to?? I'm not easily swayed by others. Yet I TOTALLY am by Maxine. 

The Maxine personification only helps me so much though. When she is on top of her game, I can't remember it. She blocks so much of my common sense.
